content.text: The images come before any director rationale, so I'll start with option a's motion sequence index.
Option a has 60 pages. I'll smoke-test the first one.

content.thinking: Frame A-000 shows a flat illustrated yard scene (house, boots, fence post device) with the caption about ankle-deep water appearing partway through; it's mostly static with a minor ground change late on. The smoke test passed, so I'll move on.
Found that in A-001 (frames 30-54), the intended flood water reads as flat bare dirt with no reflection or ripple, while the caption and static framing remain unchanged.

Clip A-002 (frames 60–84) shows the same yard with a slight push-in; at 2.2s the tag switches to "Illustration. Map marks the county" as a Texas outline with a faint county mark appears top right, while the flat brown band, lower-fence caption, and hidden boots remain unchanged.

In A-003 (frames 90-114), the caption clears at 3.2s, the boots sit in the brown band with a faint ripple ring hinting at water, a Texas outline draws in top right with a mark near the upper Gulf coast, and the tiny orange fence-post device (~10px) remains with no person and a static camera.

Frames 120-144 show a static close-up of a tilted phone with a blank screen on a porch rail, captioned "UT San Antonio says the phone warning can come after that"—all five samples identical with no motion.

I found a real state change in A-005: a "Flash Flood Warning" banner slides in at 5.2s with vibration arcs, its title clipped as "Flash Floo", and the map gains a small circle in south-central Texas by 5.8s—notably arriving after the yard flooding already appears.

Frames 180-204 show a static hold on the phone alert screen—the "Flash Floo" truncation and inland map circle near San Antonio remain unchanged, indicating about 1.2s of hold time since the alert appeared.

I noted the alert screen holds static until 7.6s before cutting to the station hero shot at 7.8s—a sensor pole with a control box partly cropped by the frame, plus a glowing yellow ring near the water at the pole's base. Continuing the frame-by-frame review from here.

In A-008 (frames 240-264), the camera tilts down and pulls back to reveal the full flood station—solar panel, control box, pole with sensor pods—against a skyline, with the map card exiting and a "Prototype flood station" callout and caption appearing by 8.6s. The caption overlaps the pole base and water-contact ring, and no researcher is shown.

Shot A-009 (frames 270–294) is a static full-station hold with its callout — a thin reflective puddle line visible in the mid park, caption placed over the pole base and brown band, no motion present.

In A-010 (frames 300-324), the station hold continues with the caption clearing at 10.4s to reveal the pole base on a concrete footing and a tiny glowing dot at the water line, otherwise a static shot.

Frames 330–354 show the station on a grassy bank by a bayou, with a sun ray hitting the solar panel and the battery bar shifting orange to green as it charges; the caption "It charges itself from light and needs no cell tower" appears, though no visual yet conveys the "no cell tower" claim.

I've logged shot A-012: the close-up holds to 12.2s before cutting to the wide park view, where a circular icon and a "No cell tower needed" callout fade in near the tower—though the claim relies solely on the text label, with no visual link or disconnection shown, and the pole base is obscured by the caption.

In A-013 (frames 390-414), I see a dashed line from the station antenna to an empty hollow ring in the sky with no satellite or receiver shown, making the destination unclear, while the "No cell tower needed" callout labels the distant tower instead. The scene stays static across these frames, with the caption positioned over the lower pole.

I've reviewed frames 420-444 (14.2-14.6s): the caption clears revealing a yellow glow at the pole's water line, then it cuts to a close-up of the three sensor pods on the slotted pole, tagged "Illustration of the described sensors," over brown water with dark blotches and a glowing yellow puck, with no caption present.

In A-015 (frames 450-474), only three of the four claimed optical sensors are clearly visible above the murky water, and a brief grass/grey strip under the water slab at 15.4-15.6s makes it look like a floating card rather than a real surface; no sensors show activity yet. I'll keep reviewing subsequent frames for these issues.

I've found that in A-016 (frames 480–504), the rising water plane submerges the lowest pod by 16.6s while two pods stay above water, but there's a finish defect where a grass/grey strip exposes the water slab's edge at frame bottom between 16.4-16.8s.

In A-017 (frames 510–534), the close-up shows weather sensor icons lighting up ("Rain", "Temperature", "Humidity", "Light"), but the caption still references "optical water sensors" until 17.6s, creating a mismatch before it clears at 17.8s.

In A-018 (frames 540-564), I see the weather box close-up cut to a labeled "Illustration. Not real hardware" circuit board diagram with a "TinyML" chip, traces, battery, and radio module, paired with the caption about the on-station AI chip; nothing animates on the board during this span.

In clip A-019 (frames 570–594), the circuit-board card stays completely static for about 1.6 seconds—no traces pulse and the chip doesn't change, so the "runs the AI itself" caption isn't actually visualized.

In A-020 (frames 600-624), I see the chip's edges glow gold at 20.2s while small white dots travel along the gold traces from the top and left inputs, converging into the chip's corner by 20.8s—a clear data-flow animation into the chip.
In frames 630-654 (A-021), the chip stays outlined but produces no output, the board shows no result, and the caption clears at 21.8s after a ~3.6s hold with ~0.6s of dot motion.

At frames 660-684 (22.6s), the board card pushes in while the caption claims it judges flood risk without a central server, but no risk output or judgment visual appears—the chip glow continues with no depiction of server absence, and the board has dominated the frame for about 4.8s.

In clip A-023 (frames 690–714), I noted the tight board shot with the amber LED and "Judged on the station" callout appearing around 23.4–23.8s—a visible output state, but one that's abstract since nothing shows what the risk level actually means, relying solely on the label to convey the lack of a central server.

In A-024 (frames 720–744), I found a cut to the wide park shot with the station's chip icon at 24.2s, a faint unidentifiable ghosted object near 24.6s, and a cryptic "No line to it" label at 24.8s that fails to visually convey "no central server" and overlaps the station's pole.

From 25.2–25.6s the station's lowest pods glow yellow for triggered sensors while the caption and grid icon remain, then it cuts to a residential street scene with a translucent brown box on the asphalt, tagged "Illustration. Ranges as described" with no caption.

Found A-026 (frames 780-804): a caption about radio signal range paired with an expanding gold ring animation from the antenna, while the street, houses, and rectangle remain static. Moving on to the next segment.

In A-027 (frames 810-834), the gold rings expand skyward from the antenna and fade by 27.6s with no receiver shown, and a tiny amber tag appears near the house at 27.8s but is too small/faint to read at phone size; the caption remains unchanged.
Frames 840-864 (A-028) show an amber "More than a half-mile" tag settling by the far house, with the rings gone and nothing else in the street carrying the signal—otherwise static, caption unchanged.

content.text: A-029 (frames 870 to 894): A static street hold. The caption clears at 29.4 s and reveals the station base with two lit lower pods. The flat brown rectangle on the road stays unchanged.

content.thinking: At 30.2s, the cut shows an open field with a small "Hub" hut and an empty fence frame, but the caption's "open country" claim is undercut by the same city skyline still visible behind it—no station is present either.

In A-031 (frames 930–954), I see a faint gold signal arc curve down to the mast behind the hub, a weak receive glow at 31.8s, and an amber "Up to five miles in open country" tag land on the fence frame, with the sending station still off-screen against the city skyline.
This hold shot (frames 960-984) shows the hub field with faint gold sky arcs and a glow at the mast top, but the hub, amber tag, and caption remain unchanged—overall the frame stays static.

Between frames 990-1014, the hub field holds until the cut at 33.8s to an interior desk scene tagged "Illustration. Not a real hub" — I notice the monitor's "Flood spread map" actually displays a line chart, not a map, and the entering sleeve appears as a disembodied arm with no visible person attached.

In A-034 (frames 1020-1044), the "map" shown is still just a line chart with yellow dots, not actual streets or flood paths, despite the caption claiming a larger AI maps flood paths—and the hand sliding along the desk edge never visibly touches anything.

In frames 1050-1074 (35.0-35.8s), I noticed the navy sleeve reads as a detached limb on the desk, and the cut to the "Flood spread map" monitor shows only a generic grid with yellow dots and brown smudges—lacking streets, creek, or houses to convey an actual flood-path map.
In A-036 (frames 1080-1104), the brown smudges remain a static orange-brown band on the chart screen rather than resolving into flood paths through streets—no responder appears in frame.

In clip A-037, I'm seeing three dashed yellow boxes highlight zones on an orange band, with "Higher risk" and "For emergency responders" labels appearing before the caption clears at 37.8s — all on an abstract chart screen with no real responder or geography shown.

Found a text-panel segment at 38.2–38.6s showing cream cards labeled "Validation accuracy" and "Field res…" over an olive background, tagged as an illustration with the caption "The university reports early chip AI validation" — no place, object, or region visible behind it.
In frames 1170-1194, the progress bar fills orange and "98.82%" appears around 39.4-39.8s, while the second card remains truncated as "Field res…" on the olive background.

Clip A-040 (frames 1200–1224) is a static hold showing the "Validation accuracy 98.82%" card with its full orange bar and the cropped "Field res…" card, caption clearing at 40.8s, with most of the frame left as empty olive space.

Found A-041 (frames 1230-1254): the same card with a slow push-in starting at 41.6s, caption restating "Accuracy was ninety eight point eight two percent" with no new visual, giving a total card hold of ~3.6s.

The card continues sliding in, with an "Initial assessments after training" note appearing at 42.4s while the second card gets pushed off the right edge—still just text-panel delivery with no visible object or location.
Found that A-043 (frames 1290–1314) shows the accuracy card and note staying fully static, with no visual change beyond the bar fill and text additions over 5.6s since 38.2s.

At A-044 (frames 1320–1344), the card stays static until 44.8s, then pans to reveal an empty "Field result" card with the caption "The announcement reports no field result" — a visual nod to the data gap, but still just a text card.

In clip A-045 (frames 1350–1374), the pan lands on the "Field result" card, where a "None reported" stamp appears at 45.4s at an angle—legible but unanchored to any place or object, while the accuracy card gets cropped at the left edge.

content.text: A-046 (frames 1380 to 1404): A static hold on the "Field result / None reported" card. The caption clears at 46.6 s and nothing else moves. The olive card section has now run about 8.6 s.

content.thinking: Found a layering defect in A-047 (frames 1410-1434): a fence post visibly bleeds through the translucent paper sheet from 47.0-47.4s before it turns opaque, revealing a labeled town grid illustration with the caption "It names no town with an installed station."

In the A-048 segment (frames 1440–1464), the town-grid map stays steady while a brief dashed circle flares into faint arcs around 48.4–48.8s over one house square—a low-contrast "searching, nothing found" effect that mostly reads as a flicker at phone size.
